subject: loosing the legend key when specifying break and level

messages.author: efb064044f1e1c0f
messages.subject: loosing the legend key when specifying break and level
parts:
Dear ggplotters,


I´m trying to create a function for doing Kaplan Meier plots in
ggplot. However I´m having trouble with allowing the function to
accept new labels for the legend. Well, actually I guess its the keys
that are missing when i specify both breaks and label. ANy ideas would
be greatly appreciated?


//M





require(survival)
require(ggplot2)

ggkm<-function(time,event,stratum,x="Days",y="Survival
Probability",lev=levels(factor(stratum))) {

stratum<-as.factor(stratum)
lev2<-levels(stratum)

m2s<-Surv(time,as.numeric(event))

fit <- survfit(m2s ~ stratum)

w<-fit$time

k<-fit$surv
o<-length(levels(stratum))
strata<-c(rep(names(fit$strata[1:o]),fit$strata[1:o]))

upper<-fit$upper
lower<-fit$lower
f<-data.frame(w,k,strata,upper,lower)

r<-ggplot (f,aes(x=w,y=k,fill=strata,group=strata))
+geom_line(aes(color=strata))
+geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper),alpha=0.3)+xlim(0,fit$maxtime)
+ylim(0,1)
r<-r+scale_fill_brewer("",palette="Set1",breaks=lev2,labels=lev)
+scale_color_brewer("",palette="Set1",breaks=lev2,labels=lev)+xlab(x)
+ylab(y)
r<-r+opts(legend.position = c(0.8,0.85))
return(r)
}


data(lung)
with(lung,ggkm(time,status,sex))

with(lung,ggkm(time,status,pat.karno))

I've thought about doing this in the past, but never actually did it.

> accept new labels for the legend. Well, actually I guess its the keys
> that are missing when i specify both breaks and label. ANy ideas would
> be greatly appreciated?

The problem is that you are specifying the breaks wrong. Since strata
is the variable that defines the color and fill, you have to use its
levels to define the breaks. Change the definition of lev2 as below
and it works. (More comments follow code).

> //M
>
> require(survival)
> require(ggplot2)
>
> ggkm<-function(time,event,stratum,x="Days",y="Survival
> Probability",lev=levels(factor(stratum))) {
>
>         stratum<-as.factor(stratum)
>         lev2<-levels(stratum)
>
>         m2s<-Surv(time,as.numeric(event))
>
>         fit <- survfit(m2s ~ stratum)
>
>         w<-fit$time
>
>         k<-fit$surv
>         o<-length(levels(stratum))
>         strata<-c(rep(names(fit$strata[1:o]),fit$strata[1:o]))

>
>         upper<-fit$upper
>         lower<-fit$lower
>         f<-data.frame(w,k,strata,upper,lower)
>
>         r<-ggplot (f,aes(x=w,y=k,fill=strata,group=strata))
> +geom_line(aes(color=strata))
> +geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=lower,ymax=upper),alpha=0.3)+xlim(0,fit$maxtime)
> +ylim(0,1)
>         r<-r+scale_fill_brewer("",palette="Set1",breaks=lev2,labels=lev)
> +scale_color_brewer("",palette="Set1",breaks=lev2,labels=lev)+xlab(x)
> +ylab(y)
>         r<-r+opts(legend.position = c(0.8,0.85))
>         return(r)
>          }
>
> data(lung)
> with(lung,ggkm(time,status,sex))
>
> with(lung,ggkm(time,status,pat.karno))

Your statement "xlim(0,fit$maxtime)" does not work because there is no
maxtime that is part of a survfit object. Did you mean "xlim(0,max(fit
$time))"?

Some other things to consider from when I was looking at this:

You will need to put in the points t=0, survival=1 in yourself. In
your examples, the difference is not noticeable, but if time to the
first event is long, the gap is there.

Consider an expand=c(0,0) on the y-axis in addition to setting the
limits to c(0,1) so that there isn't any space above 1 or below 0.
Since these are hard probabilities, nothing really "exists" past those
limits.

Have you considered how to, or do you intend to, mark censored events?

--Brian Diggs
